title: Metadichol as a Coordinated Activator of Core Cellular Machinery. Part I — Powering Up the Powerhouse: Sub-Nanomolar Metadichol Drives Coordinated Upregulation of the Complete Mitochondrial OXPHOS Gene Program in Human PBMCs
content: Background: Metadichol is a novel nanoemulsion of long-chain saturated alcohols derived from policosanol that has demonstrated pleiotropic biological activity attributed to agonism of the nuclear receptor VDR (vitamin D receptor) and other nuclear receptors. While Metadichol has been reported to modulate immune function, antioxidant pathways, and gene expression, its direct effects on mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) gene transcription remain poorly characterized.Objective: To evaluate the dose-dependent effects of Metadichol on the expression of all 13 mitochondrially encoded protein-coding genes in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), encompassing subunits of Complex I (MT-ND1–MT-ND6), Complex III (MT-CYB), Complex IV (MT-CO1–MT-CO3), and Complex V (MT-ATP6, MT-ATP8).Methods: Human PBMCs were isolated from fresh whole blood by Histopaque-1077 density gradient centrifugation and treated with Metadichol at concentrations of 0.1 pg/mL, 1 pg/mL, 100 pg/mL, 1 ng/mL, and 100 ng/mL for 24 hours. Total RNA was extracted using TRIzol reagent, reverse transcribed, and subjected to SYBR Green-based quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) using validated gene-specific primers. Relative expression was calculated using the 2-ΔΔCq method with GAPDH as reference gene.Results: Metadichol exerted a biphasic, dose-dependent effect on all 13 mitochondrial OXPHOS genes. At picogram concentrations (0.1–100 pg/mL), significant downregulation was observed for the majority of genes, with the most pronounced suppression at 1 pg/mL (mt-ND5: 0.41-fold; mt-CYB: 0.43-fold; mt-CO1: 0.54-fold; mt-ND6: 0.67-fold; all p<0.05). A notable exception was mt-ND6, which showed significant upregulation at 1 ng/mL (1.95-fold, p<0.05). At the highest concentration tested (100 ng/mL), all 13 genes were significantly upregulated relative to control, with fold-changes ranging from 1.16 (mt-CO2) to 2.41 (mt-ND6).Conclusions: These findings reveal that Metadichol orchestrates a concentration-dependent, coordinated regulation of the entire mitochondrial OXPHOS gene program in human PBMCs. The upregulation of all five mitochondrial respiratory complexes at 100 ng/mL indicates the capacity of Metadichol to enhance mitochondrial bioenergetic capacity. The biphasic profile is consistent with hormetic dose-response phenomena and may reflect engagement of nuclear receptor pathways—including VDR, PPARα, and ERRα—that coordinate PGC-1α-driven mitochondrial transcription.
